Motor guide

Comprehensive vs third-party motor insurance in Kenya

Chestnut Insurance Agency editorial team · Published 21 November 2026

Third-party cover pays for injury or damage you cause to other people and their property. Comprehensive cover does that and also protects your own vehicle against accidental damage, fire and theft. If losing the vehicle would hurt you financially, comprehensive cover is usually the safer choice.

What third-party cover does

It meets the legal minimum for third-party injury and death and typically includes third-party property damage. It does not pay to repair or replace your own vehicle.

What comprehensive adds

  • Accidental damage to your vehicle
  • Fire and theft
  • Optional extensions such as windscreen or towing, depending on the insurer

How to choose

Premium differences are driven by vehicle value, use, driver history and insurer rules. We compare options for your situation rather than quoting generic figures.

  • A newer or financed vehicle: comprehensive is normally appropriate, and lenders often require it
  • An older, low-value vehicle: third party may be acceptable if you can absorb the loss
  • Business use: declare it, and consider fleet or commercial structures

Things people overlook

  • The sum insured should reflect realistic market value
  • Excesses reduce what you receive on a claim
  • Using a private vehicle for hire without declaring it can cause trouble at claim time

This guide is general education about insurance in Kenya. It is not legal or financial advice and does not describe any specific policy. Policy wording, exclusions and the law that applies at the time govern. Speak to an advisor about your situation.
